entities.summary:
Adidas AG, founded in 1949 in Herzogenaurach, Germany, by Adolf ('Adi') Dassler, is the world's second-largest sportswear manufacturer after Nike, with annual revenues of approximately €22 billion. The Dassler family's contribution to athletic footwear is extraordinary: Adolf Dassler's brother Rudolf founded Puma in the same year — their bitter personal rivalry splitting the small Bavarian town of Herzogenaurach into two opposing camps of workers for 50 years, creating the world's two most famous athletic footwear companies from a single family's feud.

Adolf Dassler began making sports shoes in his mother's washroom in the 1920s, supplying Jesse Owens with running shoes for the 1936 Berlin Olympics — the shoes Owens wore when he won four gold medals under Hitler's gaze. The Dassler brothers worked together until their 1948 split: Adolf kept the factory, registered Adidas (from 'Adi Dassler'), while Rudolf founded Ruda (later Puma) across the Aurach river.

Adidas's iconic three stripes — purchased from Finnish company Karhu Sports in 1952 for the equivalent of €1,600 and two bottles of whisky — became one of the world's most recognized brand elements. Adidas's 2022 termination of the $1.5 billion Yeezy collaboration with Kanye West (after his antisemitic statements) created a €1 billion inventory problem, demonstrating the risks of celebrity-dependent brand strategy. The company's diversification into Reebok (acquired 2006, sold 2021) and its partnerships with Pharrell Williams and Bad Bunny represent 21st-century brand evolution.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Dassler brothers' family feud that split a single Bavarian shoe factory into Adidas and Puma — two of the world's most famous sportswear brands — is history's most commercially consequential personal rivalry.
